column1: # The bus surfaces this tree owns, and the object path each one must serve.
# binary <TAB> bus name <TAB> object path
# Fed to `dev/scripts/probe-served-objects.sh --all dev/scripts/served-objects.tsv`,
# which starts each daemon on a private bus and asks what it actually serves.
# HAND-KEPT, and that is a stated weakness rather than a design. The pairs belong
# to the call sites - the serving side names them, the calling side dials them -
# but deriving them is not a grep: ownership uses two idioms in this tree
# (`request_name` in three daemons, `connection::Builder::name` in the rest), the
# name and path are usually constants resolved per crate, and a scan by string
# SHAPE over-collects badly. `org.arlen.Transfer1` looks exactly like a bus name
# and is documented as an identifier the transfer daemon deliberately does not
# own, so a shape-built list would report correct code as broken every run.
# Deriving this properly belongs with the boot-verify job.
# Excluded on purpose:
#   org.arlen.Transfer1 - a reserved identifier, not a name anyone takes
#                         (daemons/transfer-daemon/src/request_socket.rs:30)
